ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The figure shows a chromosome schematic diagram of a cell in the body of a male mammal at a certain stage of division. Question: After this cell completes division, how many kinds of genotypes of sperm will it produce?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the circular cell in the figure, there are two pairs of homologous chromosomes, and each chromosome consists of two chromatids. The upper pair of homologous chromosomes are respectively marked D, D and d, d, with no crossing over shown. The lower pair of homologous chromosomes respectively carry A, B and a, b, and one light-colored chromatid and one dark-colored chromatid have undergone crossing over between A/a and B/b. Then reason: This is a meiotic cell of a male mammal. One primary spermatocyte can form 4 sperm after completing meiosis, and each sperm finally obtains a gene combination corresponding to one chromatid. After crossing over occurs between A/a and B/b below, the four chromatids can respectively form four combinations: AB, Ab, aB, and ab; D/d above separate during meiosis and respectively enter sperm. Since the 4 sperm finally formed by this cell correspond to chromatid combinations that are all different from each other, it will produce 4 kinds of genotypes of sperm.
